system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only voice, music-style, beat and sound-texture references condition a new sound; they do not play the original recording. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.

fragments.shot:shot-1:description: The complete supplied character reference sheet remains the actual opening image at the start of the shot, filling the frame edge to edge with its dark background, near-monochrome black-and-charcoal palette, cool blue-grey highlights, small warm amber accents, and low-key cinematic lighting unchanged. Across the top, the labeled HERO panel shows a single adult East Asian figure in a full-body view on a rain-soaked nighttime walkway. The figure stands upright between metal railings, arms relaxed at the sides, on wet reflective pavement; fine rain streaks cross the air, and soft out-of-focus warm bokeh lights glow behind the railings. The person has shaved sides and a small top-knot bun at the back of the head, with a black jacket whose chest and collar carry strap-and-buckle hardware over a dark shirt, black cargo-style trousers, and black leather lace-up combat boots with thick soles.Below the hero panel, the FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, and BACK turnaround panels keep their plain dark grey studio backdrop and even, dim lighting. The FRONT view faces the camera with a straight stance and relaxed arms; the SIDE PROFILE view turns left, showing the bun and the jacket's side silhouette; the BACK view reveals the jacket's back panel, shoulder seams, and the hair gathered at the rear of the head. The FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS detail panels remain in place with their tight close-up views: a neutral direct gaze, defined cheekbones, a small scar or mark above the left eyebrow, a metal buckle and strap with a neck zipper on the collar, two weathered hands with visible veins and knuckles, and worn black leather boots with creased toes and thick soles. The printed labels HERO, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, BACK, FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS stay legible.Within the hero panel only, the photograph comes alive with slow drifting motion: rain streaks slide gently downward, the warm lights swell and sway, wet reflections shimmer across the pavement, and the standing figure's chest rises and settles in a slow breath while the bun, collar hardware, and relaxed stance remain still. The turnaround and detail panels stay fixed and readable throughout, and the complete sheet retains its original layout, panel boundaries, subject placement, lettering, and lighting.

facts.text: A multi-panel character reference sheet on a dark background, with a labeled hero image at the top and smaller study panels arranged below.

The hero panel shows a single standing person seen in full body on a wet, dark outdoor walkway at night, with metal railings on both sides, falling rain, and blurred warm bokeh lights in the background.
The person has short hair with shaved sides and a small top-knot bun at the back of the head, and appears to be of East Asian descent.
The person wears an all-black outfit: a black jacket with strap-and-buckle details at the chest and collar, a dark shirt underneath, black cargo-style trousers, and black lace-up combat boots.
Visible on-screen labels are 'HERO', 'FRONT', 'SIDE PROFILE', 'BACK', 'FACE', 'JACKET COLLAR', 'HANDS', and 'BOOTS'.
The 'FRONT' panel shows the person standing straight, facing the camera, arms relaxed at the sides against a plain dark grey studio backdrop.
The 'SIDE PROFILE' panel shows the person in profile facing left, showing the top-knot bun and the jacket's side silhouette.
The 'BACK' panel shows the person from behind, showing the jacket's back panel and shoulder seams and the hair gathered at the back of the head.
The 'FACE' close-up shows a neutral, direct gaze, defined cheekbones, a small scar or mark above the left eyebrow, and short cropped hair on the sides.
The 'JACKET COLLAR' close-up shows a dark textured jacket collar with a metal buckle and strap and a zipper at the neck.
The 'HANDS' close-up shows two weathered hands with visible veins and knuckles resting in a dark setting.
The 'BOOTS' close-up shows worn black leather lace-up boots with thick soles and creased toes.
Lighting is low-key and cool in the hero panel, with warm accent lights behind, while the turnaround panels use even, dim studio lighting with dark grey backgrounds.
The overall palette is near-monochrome black and charcoal with cool blue-grey highlights and small warm amber light accents.

limitations: The sheet is a single composite image; the labels identify views but no camera or capture metadata is visible.
Facial identity, exact scar extent, and clothing materials are only as legible as the low-resolution panels allow.
